title: Thoreau’s cabin in the woods cost $28 and stood about two miles from his family home

cover.alt: Walden Pond in Massachusetts on a clear day: still blue water reflecting a wooded shoreline of pines and bare autumn trees.

body: On 4 July 1845 the transcendentalist Henry David Thoreau moved into a 10-by-15-foot cabin he had built beside Walden Pond, on woodland owned by his friend and mentor Ralph Waldo Emerson. He stayed two years, two months and two days, growing a garden and writing his first book. It was no wilderness exile: the cabin was about two miles from his family home in Concord, and he walked into town several times a week for news and company. His goals included simple living and self-sufficiency, and the book that came out of it, *Walden* (1854), is in part a manual for self-reliance.

slides.label: the total cost of the cabin’s materials
slides.text: Thoreau listed every item in Walden, down to the half cent. That is equivalent to about $970 in 2025.

slides.alt: A dark wooden sign under autumn trees, carved with Thoreau’s words beginning ‘I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately’.
slides.caption: Beside the stone cairn that marks where the cabin stood, a sign quotes Walden: ‘I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately’.

slides.heading: Walden, from cabin to classic
slides.note: He lived at the pond from 4 July 1845 to 6 September 1847.

slides.question: Walden is now a classic. How many copies did it sell in its first five years?
slides.explanation: It took five years to sell 2,000 copies, after it was published in Boston in August 1854.

slides.heading: Jailed over a tax
slides.text: On one of his walks into Concord, Thoreau was arrested and jailed for refusing to pay a poll tax to a state that, he wrote, ‘buys and sells men, women, and children, like cattle at the door of its senate-house’.

slides.question: Whose land did Thoreau build his cabin on?
slides.explanation: Emerson let him build a small house and plant a garden in return for clearing land on the woodlot.
